message.content: {"4": {"original": "Megaupload attracted over 50 million daily visits before the FBI seized and shut", "rephrased": "The file-sharing platform Megaupload, which drew over 50 million daily visitors, was seized by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and subsequently shut down on Thursday, resulting in the arrest and indictment of seven individuals on charges ranging from copyright infringement to racketeering and conspiracy to commit money laundering.", "summary": "Authorities report the FBI's seizure of the high-traffic Megaupload site led to seven arrests on serious federal charges."}, "5": {"original": "Megaupload allowed individuals to download movies, music, TV programs, e-books, ", "rephrased": "The seized file-sharing website Megaupload enabled users to illegally download movies, music, television programs, electronic books, and business software on a massive scale, facilitating widespread unauthorized access to copyrighted material.", "summary": "Authorities assert that the shut-down site allowed users to download vast quantities of copyrighted content illegally."}, "6": {"original": "The website was costing entertainment industry copyright-holders well in excess", "rephrased": "According to law enforcement, the operations of the Megaupload website inflicted financial damages well in excess of US$500 million on copyright-holders within the entertainment industry by enabling the mass distribution of pirated media.", "summary": "Authorities claim the site caused the entertainment industry over half a billion dollars in damages through copyright infringement."}}
